svg.aria-label: One OfficeBench subtask carried through the study: the agent reads both calendars and answers that 14:30 to 15:30 is free, which is correct; two of the four checks nonetheless require a calendar event named meeting that the task never asks anyone to create, so the run is scored FAIL and coded as a benchmark defect in all four cells.
svg.text: One subtask, four cells, four failures — and the answer was right
subtask 1-2/0, single-app calendar task, run under both models in both languages

text.tspan: Find a common time for Bob and Tom to have
an one hour zoom meeting on 5/1/2024

g.text: It says find. It does not say
the same subtask runs in all four cells
2 · The run — 4 steps of the 20 allowed

rect.data-detail: The agent never writes a file. It answers, which is what the task asked for.

g.text: The agent answers — and the answer is right
“A common time for Bob and Tom to have a one-hour zoom meeting on 5/1/2024 is from 14:30 to 15:30.”
Bob is free 14:00–16:00, Tom from 14:30 — 14:30–15:30 is the only common hour.
3 · Scoring — the benchmark’s own four checks

rect.data-detail: Requires a calendar event named "meeting" in Bob.ics. The task never asks for one to be created.
Same requirement on Tom.ics. These two checks alone decide the run.
Passes: the agent changed nothing, so nothing overlaps.
Passes: the agent changed nothing, so nothing overlaps.

g.text: Two of the four checks require a calendar event named “meeting”.
The task asked the agent to find a time, not to create one. Nothing it could
have written would satisfy the task and the check at the same time.
score agree here — 2 of 4 checks false
Yes — and it still scored FAIL
so the run indicts the benchmark, not the agent
